question: Leading late, fourth down in your own half: go for it or punt?
method: one-step engine (M2) with game-level bootstrap confidence (M3)

nfl4th_side_by_side.note: nfl4th returned NA for go_wp at yardline_100 50 and 60, so only the own 20 and own 30 can be compared.

what_one_step_cannot_capture: Clock burn after a conversion: the engine charges every converted fourth down 27 seconds and then asks the win-probability model, which knows only how such leads have turned out on average, not that this team can now run three more plays and 2 minutes off the clock.
The opponent's timeouts: they enter only through the win-probability model's timeout features, which the trees barely use. Compare the opp_timeouts_0 and opp_timeouts_3 panels.
Who gets the last possession, and the opponent scoring quickly and handing the ball back: nothing is planned beyond the next snap.
The win-probability model has its own end-game errors, cell by cell in results/m1_wp_metrics.json (test_endgame, quoted in results/m2_nfl4th_comparison.json); they affect the 2:00 panels most.
The bootstrap measures sampling noise only. A bias shared by every refit, such as the ones above, leaves boot% high and the answer still wrong.
